scope: Sivas–Tokat–Amasya axis and the eastern Anatolian Ilkhanid administrative transition

method.policy: Cross-check TDV, academic studies, institutional/official material and chronological evidence before promoting any political geometry.
rules: Do not project Eretna state borders backward into 1326.
Separate Ilkhanid sovereignty, Anatolian governor administration, local emir authority and later independent beylik control.
Use 1327 Timurtaş departure and 1335 Abu Said death as explicit temporal guards.
Do not infer exact rural boundaries from city-level administrative evidence.

anchors.name: Sivas
evidence: Academic study of Sivas attacks states Timurtaş served as Anatolian governor from 1318 to 1327 and that Sivas was the provincial center.
TDV Eretnaoğulları states Eretna became acting governor only after Timurtaş left for Egypt in 1327.
anchors.guard: Do not label Sivas Eretna state in April 1326.

anchors.name: Tokat
anchors.controlModel: Ilkhanid administration / local emirate within Ilkhanid Anatolia
evidence: TDV Tokat traces Tokat under Ilkhanid authority and places its transition to Eretna administration after Timurtaş's 1327 departure and Abu Said's 1335 death.
1314 tomb of Ilkhanid emir Nureddin b. Sentimur in Tokat provides material evidence for the Ilkhanid administrative environment.
anchors.guard: Do not assign Tokat to Eretna in 1326.

anchors.name: Amasya
anchors.controlModel: Ilkhanid administration; local authority retained as an administrative layer
evidence: TDV Amasya history places the city within the long Ilkhanid governmental period ending in 1335.
Later independent Amasya emirates are explicitly post-Ilkhanid and must not be back-projected.
anchors.guard: Do not model the later Taceddinoğlu polity in 1326; that dynasty emerged in the mid-14th century.

anchors.name: Kayseri
evidence: TDV Kayseri places Eretna's effective rule later and notes Ibn Battuta's 1332 visit while Eretna was still an Ilkhanid governor.
TDV Eretnaoğulları places Eretna's delegated administration of Kayseri after 1327.
anchors.guard: Do not use later Eretna territorial geometry for 1326.

politicalChronology.1318-1327: Timurtaş is Anatolian governor; Sivas functions as the provincial center.
politicalChronology.1326-04-07: Scenario start remains inside Timurtaş's governorship; Sivas/Tokat/Amasya/Kayseri are not Eretna independent territory.
politicalChronology.1327: Timurtaş leaves Anatolia for Egypt and leaves Alaeddin Eretna as deputy; this is the transition point for Eretna's administrative prominence.
politicalChronology.1335: Abu Said dies; Ilkhanid authority fragments and independent Eretna state formation follows.

negativeControls: Eretnaoğulları as an independent state in 1326
Later Eretna borders projected backward to 1326

runtimeModel.politicalOwner: Ilkhanid imperial authority / delegated Anatolian governor layer
runtimeModel.localAuthority: separate emir, city notables and administrative-office layer where evidence supports it
runtimeModel.tradeAndRoadNetwork: can be modeled independently from sovereignty
runtimeModel.uncertainty: retain source-level confidence and date guards
